api_usage.note: Real API usage measured from response.usage; technical duration is API/tool time, not human effort.

api_costs.basis: list-price-based estimate on real token usage; not billing-dashboard charges

personnel_cost_context.basis: literature-based context estimate, NOT measured in this experiment; no USD/EUR conversion

scenarios.source_basis: Applicon-style lower bound / major problem found and fixed

main_findings: Automatic text-similarity matching overestimates confirmed defect detection.
Total measured API cost is very low (~1.47 USD for 40 runs; list-price-based, not billing charges).
In this setup, CBR produced no additional confirmed gold-standard IDs beyond UBR; at the level of confirmed gold-standard hits, CBR was a subset of UBR.
UBR union CBR is a post-hoc result union (not a hybrid) and adds no confirmed gold coverage over UBR alone.
Low API costs make additional repetitions/variants feasible, but low cost does not imply high inspection quality.
limitations: Single model (gpt-4o-mini) and single specification; limited generalisability.
Stochastic LLM output: gold-ID composition varies across independent runs (t=0.60 includes ID 27 vs. ID 11 in old baseline).
Manual validation is a single conservative judgement-based pass.
Costs are list-price-based estimates on real usage, not billed amounts; prices must be re-checked before submission.
Personnel costs are external literature estimates, not measured here, and not currency-converted.
Automatic coverage depends on the unchanged text-similarity matcher.
